title: Website Subscription vs One-Off Build: Which Is Cheaper for UK Small Businesses?
meta_title: Website Subscription vs One-Off Build: UK Cost Guide
meta_description: Pay monthly or buy your website outright? Three-year costs side by side, what each includes, and which suits UK small businesses best in 2026.
keywords: pay monthly website vs buy outright
is a website subscription worth it

faq.q: Is a website subscription worth it?
faq.a: It's worth it if you want no upfront cost and regular changes. Over three years it often costs about the same as a one-off build plus a care plan, but with changes included.

faq.q: Do I own my website on a subscription?
faq.a: It depends on the contract. Check whether you can take your site and domain with you if you leave, and what that costs.

faq.q: How much does a one-off website cost in the UK?
faq.a: Small business websites typically cost £400 to £3,000 from budget providers and freelancers, and £3,000 to £10,000 from agencies.

faq.q: Do I still need to pay monthly after a one-off build?
faq.a: Usually yes, for hosting, security and backups. Basic care plans start at around £30 to £50 a month.
Neither on its own. What matters is fast pages, clear service pages, structured data and regular updates, which are easier when someone looks after the site every month.
